inputs.text: ABU DHABI, 16th February, 2026 (WAM) -- The National Centre of Meteorology (NCM) warned today of active to occasionally strong northwesterly winds, raising dust and sand and reducing horizontal visibility to less than 3,000 metres in some coastal and inland areas. The Centre stated in a statement issued today that the weather conditions began at 10:30 and will continue until 18:00, urging the public to exercise caution, particularly when driving on external and open roads, due to the risk of sudden drops in visibility caused by blowing dust.

requested_area.areaDesc: Coastal and inland areas, Abu Dhabi (demo zone)

fields.description: EXERCISE - Active to occasionally strong northwesterly winds are raising dust and sand, reducing visibility to under 3,000 m in some coastal and inland areas of Abu Dhabi. Until 18:00 today, 16 Feb 2026. Source: NCM.
fields.headline: EXERCISE: Blowing dust reducing visibility in coastal and inland Abu Dhabi until 18:00
fields.instruction: Take care, especially when driving on external and open roads, as visibility can drop suddenly. More: https://alerts.example.ae
left_out: No unverified inputs were received, so nothing was left out for that reason.
fields.note_for_reviewer: I set severity to Moderate and urgency to Immediate because NCM reports ongoing conditions (10:30-18:00) with visibility under 3,000 m, and the source gives no time zone (assumed local). NCM says only 'some' coastal and inland areas, while the target area was chosen by the operator, so please confirm that this alert really is exercise-only before release.

versions.description: تمرين - رياح شمالية غربية نشطة إلى قوية أحياناً تثير الغبار والرمال، مما يقلل مدى الرؤية إلى أقل من 3,000 م في بعض المناطق الساحلية والداخلية من أبوظبي. حتى الساعة 18:00 اليوم، 16 فبراير 2026. المصدر: NCM.
versions.headline: تمرين: غبار متطاير يقلل مدى الرؤية في المناطق الساحلية والداخلية من أبوظبي حتى الساعة 18:00
versions.instruction: توخوا الحذر، خاصة عند القيادة على الطرق الخارجية والمفتوحة، إذ قد ينخفض مدى الرؤية فجأة. للمزيد: https://alerts.example.ae

no_basis.concern: Severity 'Moderate' and urgency 'Immediate' are judgements the bulletin does not state explicitly, so they could be read as slightly high or low.
no_basis.searched_for: CAP severity urgency certainty definitions and NCM or WMO guidance on grading dust visibility warnings; the clauses shown give only US WEA thresholds, not a UAE or NCM grading.

WMO guidance dust storm warning visibility impact-based

payload.summary: The alert matches the NCM bulletin: same hazard (blowing dust from active to occasionally strong northwesterly winds), same visibility threshold (under 3,000 m), same areas (some coastal and inland areas), and the same end time (18:00 on 16 Feb 2026). Certainty Observed fits the bulletin, which says conditions began at 10:30 and are ongoing. Moderate severity is a reasonable reading of a visibility advisory-type warning. No unverified reports are included, and the alert is marked as an exercise.

no_basis.concern: The console_environment is 'live' while the alert is an Exercise. This is a possible mismatch, but the Exercise status matches the stated context and no clause shown addresses it.
no_basis.searched_for: rule on drill or exercise status handling in a live console environment

no_basis.concern: The WMO register entry for the UAE Meteorological Department has a blank authorization basis and a blank alerting area. It does not clearly bear on this sender, which is a demo authority.
no_basis.searched_for: UAE issuer register or authorization for the sender and area

payload.summary: The sender is in the issuer register at level 1 with wildcard areas and categories. The alert area and codes match the area drawn for event uae-dust-drill. The status Exercise fits the EXERCISE / DRILL context, and the headline is also marked EXERCISE. No active alerts from other authorities exist, so nothing is overreached. The msgType is Alert, so no references are needed.

no_basis.concern: The phone text states the hazard but gives no protective action on the first page. I could not tie this to any clause shown.
no_basis.searched_for: first page must carry hazard and action requirement in the TDRA/3GPP clauses returned

no_basis.concern: A summary of TS040 says messages should be limited to 1 page. This conflicts with the handset spec (which sets no page limit) and with 3GPP's 15 pages. The summary is not the primary specification, and the multi-page length is already recorded as gap G6.
no_basis.searched_for: TDRA page limit for UAE-Alert messages

queries: 3GPP TS 23.041 cell broadcast page limit 15 pages
TDRA cell broadcast handset specification Arabic English
UCS-2 characters per page cell broadcast 41
payload.summary: Both required languages (ar, en) are present. English is 3 pages in GSM-7 and Arabic is 5 pages in UCS-2, both well under the 15-page maximum in 3GPP TS 23.041. The encodings suit each language. The first page of each language leads with the exercise label and the hazard (winds raising dust and sand, reduced visibility). The action is not stated on the first page, but that is outside the length and delivery checks I was given. Page count is a recorded gap (G6) and is not raised again.

no_basis.concern: Arabic was machine translated without human review. This is a process point and not a meaning difference. A named Arabic reader must approve it.
no_basis.searched_for: TDRA or UAE requirement on human review of machine-translated Arabic in cell broadcast alerts

no_basis.concern: The instruction is generic (take care) and gives no specific protective action such as slowing down. The Arabic matches the English, so this is outside my mandate.
no_basis.searched_for: UAE guidance on dust alert protective actions

payload.summary: The Arabic matches the English in meaning. The EXERCISE label, hazard (blowing dust from northwesterly winds), visibility under 3,000 m, coastal and inland Abu Dhabi, the 18:00 end time, the date of 16 Feb 2026, the NCM source, the protective action (take care when driving on external and open roads, visibility can drop suddenly) and the URL are all rendered faithfully. The Arabic was machine-translated, so a named Arabic reader must still approve it before sending. This is a human sign-off step, not a difference in meaning.
